demo.title: MonoSoup evidence-based review
demo.description: Prepared PeerMind replay for a source-linked, bounded review of the supplied ICLR 2026 manuscript. Revised manuscript snapshot containing rebuttal-era CKA, ConvNeXt, and freevariance additions; original-review concerns must not be retroactively labeled false. This is a curated one-paper fixture, not a live model run. Author claims and reported results are not independently reproduced unless a deterministic check is shown. No external literature retrieval or code execution was performed. Human reviews are loaded separately and are not ground truth.

paper.title: Model Soups Need Only One Ingredient
paper.venue: Under review as a conference paper at ICLR 2026
paper.abstract: MonoSoup is presented as a data-free, post-hoc spectral reweighting method that seeks an ID–OOD balance from one fine-tuned checkpoint.

sections.title: 3 The Role of Alignment in Model Merging
Appendix H: Centered Kernel Alignment Analysis

sources.label: Abstract: single-checkpoint objective
sources.excerpt: MonoSoup is described as a simple, data-free approach using only a single checkpoint to balance ID accuracy and OOD robustness.

sources.label: Representation-collapse motivation
sources.excerpt: The paper motivates the task through the loss of general-purpose knowledge and OOD performance during fine-tuning.

sources.label: Claimed contributions
sources.excerpt: The contributions claim a geometric view of merging, Similarity-Filtered Greedy Soup, MonoSoup, and validation on vision and language benchmarks.

sources.label: Related single-model methods
sources.excerpt: Wise-FT interpolates uniformly between pretrained and fine-tuned weights; LiNeS uses post-training layer scaling and labeled data to tune hyperparameters.

sources.label: Figure 1: Similarity-Filtered Greedy Soup
sources.excerpt: The alignment-filtered soup is reported as competitive with validation-based greedy soup and the strongest single checkpoint.

sources.label: Figure 2: 2,409 pairwise combinations
sources.excerpt: Figure 2 reports an alignment analysis on 2,409 pairwise combinations of 70 CLIP ViT-B/32 checkpoints.

sources.label: Alignment interpretation
sources.excerpt: The authors observe improvements for well-aligned task vectors and diminished benefits for weakly correlated updates.

sources.label: Equations 2–3: SVD energy split
sources.excerpt: Each layer update is decomposed into high- and low-energy components; k is the smallest rank retaining fraction R of squared singular-value energy.

sources.label: Figure 3: truncation behavior
sources.excerpt: Small-task performance saturates at low rank, while the ImageNet experiment is presented as showing that truncation can reduce both ID and OOD accuracy.

sources.label: Equation 5: spectral decay
sources.excerpt: Spectral decay rho is defined from the first discarded singular value relative to the leading singular value.

sources.label: Equation 6: adaptive coefficients
sources.excerpt: The low-energy coefficient is rho plus one minus rho times cosine alpha; the high-energy coefficient is one minus the low-energy coefficient.

sources.label: Coefficient interpretation
sources.excerpt: The manuscript interprets cosine alpha as the fraction of update energy in low-energy directions and uses R as its only hyperparameter.

sources.label: Table 1: CLIP results
sources.excerpt: On the best-OOD checkpoint, average OOD rises from 50.67% to 51.60%; larger gains are reported for weak checkpoints.

sources.label: Table 2: Qwen3-0.6B results
sources.excerpt: MonoSoup is compared on GSM8K, GSM Plus, GSM8KPlatinum, SciQ, and MMLU-Pro-Math using three fine-tuning variants.

sources.label: Language ID/OOD protocol
sources.excerpt: GSM8K and SciQ are treated as ID, while GSM Plus, GSM8KPlatinum, and MMLU-Pro-Math are treated as OOD or more challenging benchmarks.

sources.label: Figure 4: Wise-FT complement
sources.excerpt: MonoSoup plus Wise-FT is reported to produce a stronger ID–OOD Pareto frontier across five ImageNet shifts.

sources.label: Figure 5: R sensitivity
sources.excerpt: Performance is reported as stable across a range of R values, but the method still requires selecting the variance threshold.

sources.label: Stated limitations
sources.excerpt: The paper says R may require adaptation across architectures or domains and that broader architectures and stronger theoretical grounding remain future work.

sources.label: Conclusion claim
sources.excerpt: The conclusion claims robust gains from a lightweight single-model procedure across vision and language domains.

sources.label: Table 3: extended CLIP comparison
sources.excerpt: Extended comparisons show the strongest benefits on representation-collapsed checkpoints and smaller changes on strong checkpoints.

sources.label: Figure 6: rank ablation
sources.excerpt: Rank ablations contrast the 20-task benchmark with ImageNet fine-tuning and expose regime-dependent behavior.

sources.label: Appendix G: boundary-condition argument
sources.excerpt: The coefficient is characterized as the simplest bilinear function satisfying four chosen boundary conditions and as monotone and 1-Lipschitz.

sources.label: Appendix H: CKA analysis
sources.excerpt: CKA results for two CLIP checkpoints are used to associate low-energy directions with preserving pretrained OOD representations.

sources.label: Figures 10–11: threshold sensitivity
sources.excerpt: R sensitivity is shown for two CLIP checkpoints and a ConvNeXt checkpoint, with different response shapes.

sources.label: Table 5: ConvNeXt results
sources.excerpt: ConvNeXt results report 85.17/55.85 ID/OOD for fine-tuning, 85.19/56.07 for freevariance, and 85.57/56.70 for R=0.8.

sources.label: Figure 12: all 70 checkpoints
sources.excerpt: A quiver plot displays movement in ID and OOD performance after applying MonoSoup to all 70 CLIP checkpoints.

sources.label: Section 5.2: claimed +9.2 language gains
sources.excerpt: The text claims that the largest gains on GSM Plus and GSM8K Platinum are +9.2 points each.

sources.label: Appendix C: dependence between R and cosine alpha
sources.excerpt: The appendix derives cosine-squared alpha = 1 - P_k, where P_k is the spectral energy retained by the high-energy component selected using R.

sources.label: Equation 6: complementary coefficient constraint
sources.excerpt: The method sets lambda Low = rho + (1-rho) cosine alpha and lambda High = 1 - lambda Low, forcing the two coefficients to sum to one.

sources.label: Section 3 to Section 4 mechanism transition
sources.excerpt: The multi-model analysis measures cosine similarity between distinct task vectors, while MonoSoup transitions to an SVD decomposition of one task vector.

paperSummary.overview: Fine-tuning can trade OOD robustness for target-task specialization, while model soups require multiple checkpoints. MonoSoup decomposes each fine-tuning update with SVD and reweights high- and low-energy components using layer-wise spectral quantities.

keyPoints.title: Problem
keyPoints.summary: Fine-tuning can trade OOD robustness for target-task specialization, while model soups require multiple checkpoints.

keyPoints.title: Approach
keyPoints.summary: MonoSoup decomposes each fine-tuning update with SVD and reweights high- and low-energy components using layer-wise spectral quantities.

keyPoints.title: Reported evidence
keyPoints.summary: CLIP/ImageNet natural shifts; Qwen3-0.6B reasoning benchmarks; Wise-FT combinations; CKA on two CLIP checkpoints; ConvNeXt results; rank and threshold ablations

keyPoints.title: Claimed contributions
keyPoints.summary: Same-task update-alignment analysis; Similarity-Filtered Greedy Soup; Single-checkpoint spectral reweighting; Vision and language evaluation

review.overallAssessment: A practical and clearly structured single-checkpoint method with useful empirical evidence. The central concern is that the paper's alignment narrative does not match the residual-energy quantity used by MonoSoup, while the imposed coefficient constraint leaves a layer-wise shrinkage explanation unisolated. The review also identifies bounded contribution, OOD-scope, scale, uncertainty, and numerical-reporting issues. Architecture coverage is present in the revised snapshot and is not treated as an original-review false positive.
strengths: Simple layer-wise construction with broad source traceability.
Experiments cover vision, language, a non-Transformer architecture, and multiple ablations.
The supplied appendix adds useful coefficient and representation analysis.
authorQuestions: Use bounded cross-benchmark language or add a controlled distribution-shift protocol.
Add at least one multi-billion-parameter experiment with accuracy and end-to-end resource measurements.
Disclose the six exclusions and their effect on the alignment analysis.
Rename the quantity residual-energy share and treat CKA preservation as a separate empirical observation, or define and validate an actual alignment measure.
Compare against layer-wise scalar shrinkage matched to MonoSoup's update norm and ablate the sum-to-one constraint.
Present Section 3 as inspiration unless a direct mapping between pairwise alignment and single-update spectral statistics is demonstrated.
Recompute every Table 2 delta, name the comparison baseline, and replace the +9.2 statement with traceable values.

findings.critique: The single-checkpoint setting is practically useful, but the paper does not establish how much of the algorithmic contribution goes beyond existing SVD-based editing and scaling methods.

contract.scope: Stated contributions and paper-internal related-work comparison

contract.stopRule: Do not declare the method non-novel without external literature verification.

evidenceFor.summary: The paper itself describes related single-model scaling and SVD-adjacent approaches, while its core operation remains spectral decomposition and reweighting.

evidenceAgainst.summary: The one-checkpoint, data-free robustness objective and geometry-to-method framing are clearly differentiated at the problem-setting level.

missingEvidence: Externally verified, operation-level comparison with the closest spectral methods.

importance.explanation: Contribution positioning affects the central publication claim.

sensitivity.explanation: External literature adjudication is outside this paper-only fixture.

limitations: Paper-internal evidence cannot establish priority.
findings.nextAction: Add a compact taxonomy and controlled comparisons against the closest SVD-based post-hoc methods.

findings.critique: The boundary-condition derivation gives the coefficient useful mathematical properties, but it does not show that the chosen conditions are necessary for OOD robustness or that the rule is optimal.

contract.allegation: The explanatory claim exceeds the derivation.
contract.falsifier: A risk-based derivation or comparison showing why these conditions identify the robustness-preserving rule.
contract.evidenceBurden: Preserve the valid bilinear uniqueness, monotonicity, and Lipschitz results.
contract.stopRule: Do not demand convergence for a one-shot transformation.

evidenceFor.summary: The appendix explicitly limits optimality and derives uniqueness only after selecting four boundary conditions and a bilinear family.

evidenceAgainst.summary: The paper establishes monotonicity, 1-Lipschitz sensitivity, and supplies CKA evidence consistent with its interpretation.

missingEvidence: A theory connecting spectral statistics to ID/OOD risk.
Comparison with alternative admissible coefficient families.

importance.explanation: The weighting rule is the central mechanism.

sensitivity.explanation: A substantive theory cannot be simulated as a wording change.

limitations: The empirical mechanism may still be useful without a full theory.
findings.nextAction: State the rule as a constrained design choice or add risk-based theory and competing-rule ablations.

findings.critique: The categorical allegation that the current supplied manuscript contains no non-Transformer evidence is false, although that concern was valid for the original submission and the revised automatic-selection procedure remains underdocumented.

contract.allegation: Non-Transformer evidence is absent from the current supplied snapshot.
contract.scope: Current PDF main text and appendices; original-review timing recorded separately
contract.falsifier: Locate a non-Transformer experiment in the current snapshot.
contract.evidenceBurden: Search appendices and preserve the chronology of added evidence.
contract.stopRule: Refute only the current-snapshot absence allegation; do not retroactively characterize the original reviewer concern as false.

evidenceFor.summary: The main discussion calls R the only hyperparameter and acknowledges architecture/domain dependence.

evidenceAgainst.summary: The appendix evaluates ConvNeXt and reports a freevariance variant alongside R=0.8.

missingEvidence: A clear definition and reproducible procedure for the briefly labeled freevariance variant.

importance.explanation: The categorical current-snapshot absence claim is false, while the original concern was resolved through revision rather than reviewer error.

sensitivity.explanation: Removing the rebuttal-era appendix records recreates the original evidence gap; unrelated result changes do not.

limitations: The appendix terminology is terse and one ConvNeXt family does not establish broad architectural coverage.
This verdict applies only to the revised supplied PDF.
findings.nextAction: Record the concern as resolved after revision, formally specify freevariance, and expand architecture coverage.

findings.critique: The language evaluation labels harder or different tasks as OOD without isolating distribution shift, so it supports cross-benchmark generalization but not a clean OOD-robustness conclusion.

contract.allegation: The language OOD interpretation is broader than the protocol supports.
contract.falsifier: A controlled shift holding capability and difficulty fixed or an explicit bounded claim.
contract.evidenceBurden: Do not invalidate the reported benchmark accuracies.
contract.stopRule: Retain results as descriptive cross-benchmark evidence.

evidenceFor.summary: The ID/OOD grouping mixes training overlap, task identity, and increased difficulty.

evidenceAgainst.summary: The reported results still show gains across several reasoning and multiple-choice benchmarks.

missingEvidence: Controlled linguistic, domain, or corruption shifts for the language model.

importance.explanation: OOD robustness is a headline claim.

sensitivity.explanation: Narrowing the claim to cross-benchmark generalization resolves the scope concern; unrelated numerical formatting does not.

limitations: This finding concerns interpretation, not arithmetic correctness of Table 2.
findings.nextAction: Use bounded cross-benchmark language or add a controlled distribution-shift protocol.

findings.critique: The manuscript motivates MonoSoup through large-model checkpoint cost but provides no accuracy, runtime, peak-memory, or storage profile at the 2–7B+ scale where the claimed advantage is most consequential.

contract.allegation: The practical scale claim lacks direct evidence.
contract.scope: Efficiency motivation and evaluated model sizes
contract.falsifier: End-to-end quality and resource measurements on at least one multi-billion-parameter model.
contract.evidenceBurden: Acknowledge that one checkpoint logically avoids training a checkpoint ensemble.
contract.stopRule: Do not fabricate hardware costs or infer failure at scale.

evidenceFor.summary: The largest language experiment uses Qwen3-0.6B and the supplied PDF contains no measured wall-clock or memory table.

evidenceAgainst.summary: Using one fine-tuned checkpoint plainly removes the need to train and retain dozens of soup constituents.

missingEvidence: 2–7B+ quality experiment.
Measured SVD runtime, peak memory, storage, and comparison protocol.

importance.explanation: The gap bears directly on the practical motivation.

sensitivity.explanation: The required scale experiment is unavailable in this baseline manuscript.

limitations: Absence of evidence is not evidence that the method fails to scale.
findings.nextAction: Add at least one multi-billion-parameter experiment with accuracy and end-to-end resource measurements.

findings.critique: Figure 2 reports 2,409 pairs from 70 checkpoints, but 70 choose 2 equals 2,415 and no six-pair exclusion is disclosed.

contract.allegation: A six-pair reporting discrepancy is unexplained.
contract.falsifier: A disclosed exclusion rule accounting for exactly six pairs.
contract.stopRule: Keep the verdict local; do not imply fabrication or invalidate the experiment.

evidenceFor.summary: The figure reports 2,409 combinations; deterministic calculation gives 70 × 69 ÷ 2 = 2,415.

missingEvidence: Identity of the six excluded pairs and whether exclusion changes the summary.

importance.explanation: This is a bounded reporting issue unless the excluded cases materially affect results.

sensitivity.explanation: Adding an exact exclusion disclosure repairs the finding; unrelated prose does not.

limitations: The calculation alone cannot determine why six pairs are absent.
findings.nextAction: Disclose the six exclusions and their effect on the alignment analysis.

findings.critique: The strongest-checkpoint improvements are modest and are reported without variability estimates, making statistical reliability difficult to assess even though weak checkpoints improve substantially.

contract.allegation: Small strong-baseline gains are insufficiently uncertainty-qualified.
contract.falsifier: Repeated-run uncertainty or a deterministic evaluation argument showing the differences are stable.
contract.stopRule: Do not call reported point estimates false.

evidenceFor.summary: The best-OOD gain is 0.93 percentage points and no standard deviations or confidence intervals are reported.

evidenceAgainst.summary: Weak checkpoints show much larger recovery and Figure 12 visualizes behavior across all 70 checkpoints.

missingEvidence: Run-to-run variability or uncertainty intervals.
Aggregate effect-size statistics over the 70 checkpoints.

importance.explanation: Uncertainty affects claims of consistent improvement over strong alternatives.

sensitivity.explanation: Adding stable repeated-run estimates would weaken the concern; unrelated wording would not.

limitations: Checkpoint evaluation may be deterministic, but fine-tuning and selection variability still matter.
findings.nextAction: Report uncertainty and aggregate effect sizes, separated for strong and collapsed checkpoints.

findings.critique: The quantity named cosine alpha is a normalized residual-energy magnitude, not a cosine alignment between the low-energy update and pretrained weights; describing it as alignment or a pretrained-preservation signal overstates what its definition establishes.

contract.allegation: The semantic interpretation of cosine alpha does not follow from its mathematical definition.
contract.scope: Equation 6, Appendix C, and the CKA interpretation
contract.falsifier: Identify the two objects whose inner product defines the claimed alignment, or revise the terminology to residual-energy share.
contract.evidenceBurden: Separate the exact identity from the empirical CKA correlation.
contract.stopRule: Do not claim the empirical correlation is false; limit the verdict to what the formula proves.

evidenceFor.summary: Appendix C explicitly derives cosine-squared alpha as 1 - P_k, the fraction of update energy outside the retained subspace.
The prose nevertheless describes the quantity as alignment and as a pretrained-preservation signal without defining a cosine with pretrained parameters or representations.

evidenceAgainst.summary: The CKA analysis supplies empirical evidence that models retaining more low-energy structure can remain closer to pretrained representations on selected inputs.

missingEvidence: A genuine geometric alignment definition involving two specified vectors.
Evidence that residual-energy share predicts representation preservation beyond the selected CKA cases.

importance.explanation: The alignment story is the stated bridge from the diagnostic analysis to the proposed method.

sensitivity.explanation: Renaming the quantity and narrowing the causal interpretation repairs the semantic defect without changing the algorithm.

limitations: This verdict does not show that the coefficient is ineffective.
findings.nextAction: Rename the quantity residual-energy share and treat CKA preservation as a separate empirical observation, or define and validate an actual alignment measure.

findings.critique: The manuscript presents spectral decay and cosine alpha as complementary signals, but both are functions of the same singular-value spectrum and cosine-squared alpha is constrained directly by the R-selected retained energy.

contract.allegation: The claimed complementarity is not quantitatively established.
contract.scope: Definitions of R, rho, and cosine alpha plus the component ablation
contract.falsifier: Show that cosine alpha supplies predictive information beyond R, retained rank, and rho across layers and checkpoints.
contract.evidenceBurden: Do not equate statistical dependence with total redundancy.
contract.stopRule: Preserve the component-ablation result while requesting an incremental-information analysis.

evidenceFor.summary: Because cosine-squared alpha = 1 - P_k and P_k is selected using R, the value is tightly constrained by the threshold and spectrum.

evidenceAgainst.summary: The component ablation reports different empirical behavior when using rho alone versus cosine alpha alone.

missingEvidence: Layer-wise correlations among R, retained rank, rho, and cosine alpha.
Incremental predictive or ablation evidence controlling for update magnitude.

importance.explanation: The method is motivated as combining two complementary geometric signals.

sensitivity.explanation: A controlled incremental-information analysis can directly support or weaken the concern.

limitations: Two spectrum-derived statistics can still capture different aspects of spectral shape.
findings.nextAction: Report correlations and controlled ablations showing what information cosine alpha contributes beyond R, rank, and rho.

findings.critique: Forcing lambda High plus lambda Low to equal one scales both spectral components below their fine-tuned coefficients of one, so the reported gains may partly arise from layer-wise shrinkage toward the pretrained model rather than spectral separation itself.

contract.allegation: The experiments do not isolate spectral reweighting from induced update shrinkage.
contract.scope: Equation 6 and comparisons with interpolation baselines
contract.falsifier: A matched layer-wise scalar baseline with the same update norm performs materially worse, or an independent-coefficient ablation supports the constraint.
contract.evidenceBurden: Acknowledge that Wise-FT tests global rather than matched layer-wise shrinkage.
contract.stopRule: Do not claim shrinkage fully explains the gains without the requested baseline.

evidenceFor.summary: The coefficients sum to one, whereas the unedited fine-tuned update uses coefficient one on both high- and low-energy components.

evidenceAgainst.summary: Wise-FT and component ablations provide partial evidence that uniform interpolation and individual signals behave differently.

missingEvidence: Layer-wise norm-matched scalar shrinkage baseline.
Ablation allowing high- and low-energy coefficients to vary independently.
Update-norm statistics by layer.

importance.explanation: Without this control, the experiment does not identify which part of the proposed mechanism causes the gain.

sensitivity.explanation: The decisive matched baseline requires a new experiment.

limitations: The concern identifies an alternative explanation; it does not establish that shrinkage is sufficient.
findings.nextAction: Compare against layer-wise scalar shrinkage matched to MonoSoup's update norm and ablate the sum-to-one constraint.

findings.critique: Section 3 studies cosine alignment between distinct same-task model updates, while MonoSoup operates on the singular spectrum of one update; the manuscript does not establish the implication connecting these different objects.

contract.allegation: The multi-model analysis motivates the problem but does not derive the single-model mechanism.
contract.falsifier: A formal or empirical mapping showing that the single-update statistics predict the pairwise alignment behavior relevant to successful soups.
contract.evidenceBurden: Preserve Section 3 as valid empirical evidence about same-task merging.
contract.stopRule: Do not require the motivational analysis to be a theorem; require the narrative claim to match its support.

evidenceFor.summary: The diagnostic uses cosine similarity between two task vectors, but the proposed method replaces that relation with energy statistics of one task vector.

evidenceAgainst.summary: Both analyses support the broader intuition that directional structure in fine-tuning updates matters for generalization.

missingEvidence: Cross-check that single-model spectral statistics predict pairwise merge success or soup-like directions.
A narrower statement separating inspiration from derivation.

importance.explanation: The claimed geometric bridge is central to the paper's novelty narrative.

sensitivity.explanation: Narrowing the claim from derivation to inspiration resolves the logical overreach; a substantive mapping could support the stronger claim.

limitations: A method may work even when its motivating analogy is incomplete.
findings.nextAction: Present Section 3 as inspiration unless a direct mapping between pairwise alignment and single-update spectral statistics is demonstrated.

findings.critique: The statement that GSM Plus and GSM8K Platinum each improve by +9.2 points is not supported by the Table 2 fine-tuned-to-MonoSoup differences and lacks a clearly stated alternative reference baseline.

contract.allegation: A narrative effect-size claim cannot be reconciled with its cited table.
contract.falsifier: Identify the exact rows, columns, aggregation, and baseline producing +9.2 on both named benchmarks.
contract.evidenceBurden: Check all plausible within-variant baselines before declaring a discrepancy.
contract.stopRule: Mark the claim unexplained rather than guessing the intended comparison.

evidenceFor.summary: The visible within-variant changes are approximately 0.5–1.5 points, and the prose does not specify a different calculation yielding +9.2 for both benchmarks.

missingEvidence: Exact provenance for each +9.2 value.
A corrected effect-size statement if the claim is erroneous.

sensitivity.explanation: Correcting the values or adding a reproducible baseline calculation resolves the finding; unrelated prose does not.

limitations: PDF text extraction can merge table cells, so final correction should be checked against source data.

report.summary: Promising and practical, with credible empirical breadth in the supplied manuscript. The central geometric explanation should be revised because residual-energy share is not itself an alignment measure, and a matched shrinkage control is needed to identify the mechanism. Stronger theoretical positioning, a cleaner language OOD protocol, large-scale resource evidence, uncertainty reporting, and two numerical corrections are also needed.

response.answer: For each layer, the method forms the fine-tuning update, splits it with SVD at an energy threshold, and applies adaptive coefficients derived from spectral decay and low-energy mass before adding the edit back to pretrained weights.

Appendix G establishes uniqueness only inside a chosen bilinear family and shows monotonic, Lipschitz behavior. It does not establish that the boundary conditions are necessary for robustness or that the rule optimizes ID/OOD risk.

Pages 21–22 contain a ConvNeXt threshold ablation and Table 5 reports ConvNeXt results, including a freevariance variant. That evidence refutes the categorical claim that the supplied manuscript is Transformer-only.
The number of unordered pairs is n(n−1)/2. For n=70, 70×69/2=2,415. Figure 2 reports 2,409, leaving six pairs unexplained.

Appendix C derives cosine-squared alpha as one minus the retained spectral-energy fraction. That is a normalized magnitude, not an inner-product alignment with pretrained weights. The CKA result is separate empirical evidence and does not change the definition.

The prose reports +9.2 points on two benchmarks, but the visible fine-tuned-to-MonoSoup changes in Table 2 are roughly 0.5–1.5 points. No alternative rows or baseline are named that reproduce +9.2 for both tasks.

humanReviews.label: Reviewer mj9q
humanReviews.reviewText: The paper is practical and conceptually elegant, but the novelty beyond SVD-based methods is limited, the coefficient lacks theoretical grounding, and the soup terminology may overstate the relation to ensembling.

humanReviews.label: Reviewer YMQp
humanReviews.reviewText: The method is lightweight and empirically strong, but the single-checkpoint storage motivation is unconvincing and evidence on another modality such as audio would strengthen applicability.

humanReviews.label: Reviewer q1EA
humanReviews.reviewText: The coefficient interpretation is unclear, Figure 3 may conflict with the truncation narrative, gains over LiNeS are marginal without variability, generality may be regime-dependent, and Figure 2 has a pair-count discrepancy.

humanReviews.label: Reviewer gzvH
humanReviews.reviewText: The creative single-checkpoint reframing is strong, but plug-and-play practicality is qualified by selecting R, architecture diversity is limited, and a label-free selection rule is needed.

humanReviews.label: Reviewer Yqvj
humanReviews.reviewText: The method is simple and well motivated, but gains on strong checkpoints are modest, variability is missing, and the per-layer impact of the coefficients needs deeper analysis.

baselineReview.label: ChatGPT independent review
baselineReview.reviewText: An independent long-form review emphasizing coefficient semantics, signal dependence, update shrinkage, the Section 3-to-4 bridge, language effect-size arithmetic, SVD cost, aggregate CLIP statistics, and presentation accuracy.
